summary: 尼安德特人因地制宜，在有洞穴和缺洞穴的地区采用不同栖身方式。文章比较露天遗址、洞内结构和火堆痕迹，也提醒读者区分人工安排和自然形成的图案。
logic: 检验穴居人的常见印象

sentences: We think of our prehistoric ancestors as people of the ice and snow, living in caves, and for many of the West European Neanderthalers that is just a picture of their life.
我们把史前的祖先视为冰雪中的人，生活在洞穴中，对许多西欧尼安德特人来说，仅仅是他们生活的一幅图。
But where there were no caves, further to the east on the Russian steppe, for example, open-air sites with some sort of constructed shelter were the only option.
但是，在俄罗斯草原东边没有洞穴的地方，例如，只有露天场地和某种建造的掩体是唯一的选择。

We now know much more about the cave sites than the open-air ones because, historically, it was the cave sites of Western Europe that were first explored by archaeologists and also because open-air sites are harder to find – many of them have disappeared under deep mud deposits or under the rising postglacial seas.
我们现在对洞穴地点的了解比对露天地点的了解要多得多，因为历史上，是西欧的洞穴地点首先由考古学家进行探索，而且由于露天地点更难找到——其中许多是在深层泥土矿床或不断上升的冰川后海洋中消失的。
Caves, moreover, aid the survival of archaeological material and can preserve the records of remote millennia.
此外，洞穴有助于考古材料的生存，并能够保存几千年的偏远记录。
In south-west France, the limestone caves of the Périgord region made ideal homes for the Neanderthal people.
在法国西南部，Périgod地区的石灰岩洞为尼安德特人提供了理想的家园。
There were good supplies of flint to hand for axes and the like, and the caves were often sited in small river valleys that offered protection against the worst of the weather.
有大量的石供应用于斧头等，洞穴通常位于小河谷中，提供了保护

The Neanderthalers liked south-facing caves, for obvious reasons of sunshine and wind avoidance, and caves at some height above the valley floor offered refuge from floods and good game-watching vantage points.
尼安德特人喜欢南面的洞穴，明显的原因阳光和避免风，和山顶高处的洞穴提供了避难所洪水和良好的看球优势。
The Périgord region during the last ice age was, in fact, an exceptionally benign habitat for humans.
事实上，在上一个冰河时期，Périgord地区是人类极为温和的栖息地。

It enjoyed a rather maritime climate with cooler summers that permitted the extension of tundra and steppe over its higher plateaux, and its year-round high levels of sunshine favoured the growth of the ground plants needed by reindeer, bison and horse.
它拥有较凉爽的夏季海洋气候，能够将苔原和大草原延伸到高原，其全年高温的阳光有利于驯鹿、野牛和马所需的地面植物的生长。
Winters were mildish for the ice age, animals never needed to migrate far from summer to winter, and men never needed to travel far from home to find abundant supplies of meat.
冬天对冰河时代来说是温和的，动物从不需要从夏天迁徙到冬天，男人也不需要远走高飞寻找大量的肉类。

In Central and Eastern Europe, where caves are less readily available, such open-air sites as have been discovered were mostly located near water: bottom-land was a good area to be for people and animals, and also because the sedimentation pattern of lakes and stream courses has aided archaeological preservation – whereas erosion has presumably blown away sites which were out in the open.
在中欧和东欧，洞穴不那么容易找到，所发现的露天地点大多位于水边：底层是人类和动物的好地方，而且湖泊和溪流流的沉积模式有助于考古保护，而侵蚀大概已经把露天的遗址吹走。
Some of the open-air sites in Germany, Central Europe and Russia have provided valuable information about Neanderthal man and his way of life.
德国、中欧和俄罗斯的一些露天场所提供了关于尼安德特人及其生活方式的宝贵信息。

From Moldova, for example, comes evidence that has been interpreted as the remains of wind-breaks, or even a large tent-ring, up to about 8 x 5 m in size, of mainly mammoth bones enclosing a dense concentration of stone tools, animal bones and ash.
例如，从摩尔多瓦得到的证据被解释为风破碎的残骸，甚至一个大帐篷环，其大小约为8x5米，主要是长毛象骨头，其中含有密集的石器、动物骨头和灰。
From the West European caves more evidence of built structures is available, and some of it goes back a long way in time.
从西欧洞穴可以找到更多建筑结构的证据，其中有些可以追溯到很久以前。

In the Grotte du Lazaret, near Nice, at a date during the last ice age but one, claims for some sort of skin tent within the cave have been advanced, on the basis of arrangements of large stones out from the cave wall that might have supported timber struts for a covering of skins up to the rock face above.
在尼斯附近的Grotte du Lazaret，在上次冰河时代的一个日子，声称在洞穴里有某种皮肤帐篷已经进步了，依据是山洞墙上的大块石头可能支撑了木材的柱子覆盖上面的岩石面

At Lazaret, what might be openings in the hypothesised tents seem to point away from the cave mouth, and finds of wolf and fox foot bones, without the rest of the skeletons, inside these ‘tents’ have been thought to indicate the use of animal pelts as bed coverings.
在拉扎雷特，假想的帐篷的开口似乎指向洞口，发现在这些“帐篷”内没有其他骨骼的狼和狐狸脚骨，被认为是用动物皮作为床盖。

The two patches of ash at Lazaret that mark ancient fires, with stone tools around them evidently made and used on the spot, are edged with small marine mollusc shells, prompting the excavator to suggest that seaweed had been used as bedding around the fires.
拉扎雷特的两块灰片标记了古老的火灾，周围显然有石器，并当场使用，这些灰片被小型海洋软体壳壳覆盖，促使挖土机表明海藻是作为火堆的掩体。

The cave of Baume-Bonne in the Basses-Alpes region of France, another early site, boasts ten square metres of cobbles brought up from the local river and laid down, as though to take care of a puddle area in the cave, with the smoothest and roundest surfaces of the stones uppermost, and there are other similar cases.
法国巴西斯-阿尔卑斯地区的Baume-Bonne洞穴是另一个早期的遗址，有10平方米的椰子从当地河流中浮出并沉淀下来，似乎可以处理洞穴中的一个水坑区，石头的最上层是最平滑和最圆的表面，还有其他类似的情况。

The ash encountered in concentrations at some sites testifies to the Neanderthal people’s use of fire: not surprising, since use of fire was, by Neanderthal times, an already ancient accomplishment of evolving humanity, and survival in the sub-arctic conditions faced by the Neanderthalers is inconceivable without control of fire.
在一些地点聚集的灰烬证明了尼安德特人使用火：毫不奇怪，因为尼安德特时代，使用火已经是人类不断演变的古老成就，而尼安德特人在亚北极条件下的生存如果没有火灾的控制是不可思议的。
Fire gave warmth, light, heat for cooking and defence against predatory animals.
火提供了温暖、光线、烹饪热和防食动物。
A charred piece of birch from Krapina in Croatia is thought to be the remains of a fire-making twirl stick.
据信克罗地亚克拉皮纳的一块烧焦的燃烧石是火力棒的残骸。
But Neanderthal hearths, in the sense of specially constructed places for fire, are fewer and harder to identify with certainty than the mere ash piles that are a regular feature of their sites.
但是尼安德特人的灵洞，从特别建造的火灾地点的意义上来说，比起其地点通常具有的灰堆，越来越难以肯定地识别。
They seem often to have just lit a small fire (40–50 cm across) on the existing ground surface of the cave, without preparation.
他们似乎经常在洞穴现有地面点燃一小股火(40-50厘米对面)，而没有做好准备。
Judging from the shallow penetration of heat effects under the ash, this fire was only of short duration.
从灰烬下热效应的浅渗透来看，这种火灾只是短暂的。
Sometimes the fires were larger in size, up to one metre across, and quite irregular in shape.
有时大火更大，高达一米，形状相当不正常。

It is not always easy to decide how much additional structure some fires possessed: claims of stone circles to contain the fire run up against the fact that stones tend to litter the cave floors everywhere and those around a fire can quite accidentally look as though they were arranged in a circle.
通常很难确定一些火灾有多少额外的结构：声称有石圈控制着火灾，而事实上，石头往往到处乱扔洞穴地板，而周围的人则会意外地看起来好像是被安排在一个圆圈里。

items.answer: iii · A perfect place to live
items.cue: 在法国西南部，Périgod地区的石灰岩洞为尼安德特人提供了理想的家园。
items.why: 法国佩里戈尔有燧石、朝南洞穴和较温和的气候，也利于获得动物资源。

items.zh: 为 C 段选择最能概括全段的标题。

items.why: 中东欧洞穴较少，摩尔多瓦等地的露天遗址留下了可能属于住所的痕迹。

items.why: 研究者从灰堆、石块和疑似出入口等遗迹，推断洞内的人为布局。

items.answer: vi · A vital source of power
items.cue: 在一些地点聚集的灰烬证明了尼安德特人使用火：毫不奇怪，因为尼安德特时代，使用火已经是人类不断演变的古老成就，而尼安德特人在亚北极条件下的生存如果没有火灾的控制是不可思议的。
items.why: 火提供照明、取暖、烹饪和防护，炉火遗迹也帮助推断它的实际使用方式。

a circular arrangement of animal bones
evidence suggesting the use of animal fur for warmth
items.zh: 有证据表明动物毛皮可以用来取暖

items.en: The use of fire Neanderthalers could not have survived without fire because the conditions they lived in were ________.
items.zh: 尼安德特人生活的环境属于 ________，没有火就无法生存。
items.why: 说明没有火在“亚北极条件” 下无法生存。

items.en: Most evidence of purpose-built fires takes the form of ash piles, features of which suggest that the fires lasted a ________ time.
items.zh: 人工生火留下的证据大多是灰堆，从灰堆的特征可以推断，火持续燃烧的时间较 ________。
items.why: 回到对应内容“从灰烬下热效应的浅渗透来看，这种火灾只是短暂的”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: It is hard to be certain about the size and structure of the fires, though they were certainly needed to protect the occupants from dangerous ________, among other things.
items.zh: 火堆究竟多大、怎样搭成，很难确定，但防范危险的 ________ 确实是用火的目的之一。
items.why: 明确指出火用于抵御“食肉 /掠食动物”。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空最多填两个词。

items.en: The purpose of the writer of this article is to
correct: discuss what is known about Neanderthal settlements.
讨论关于尼安德特人定居点的已知情况

pairs: 题干用动词，定位句改用同词根的名词。
points: 作者把洞穴与无洞可住时建造的露天住所并置，又解释为何洞穴留下的证据更多。
回到对应内容“从灰烬下热效应的浅渗透来看，这种火灾只是短暂的”，再按题干要求写出答案。
clauses: It enjoyed a rather maritime climate with cooler summers …, and its year-round high levels of sunshine favoured the growth of the ground plants needed by reindeer, bison and horse.
“that permitted the extension of tundra and steppe over its higher plateaux”修饰前面的 climate。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 that 时，回看 climate，再把修饰信息接回主句。
We now know much more about the cave sites than the open-air ones … – many of them have disappeared under deep mud deposits or under the rising postglacial seas.
连接词 because 引出“because, historically, it was the cave sites of Western Europe that were first explored by archaeologists and also because open-air sites are harder to find”，说明主句的原因关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 because 把这一层关系补进去。
